title: Fractions
description: Class 5 IMO — Fractions: comparing unlike fractions, adding and subtracting mixed fractions, multiplying fractions, dividing fractions, and fraction word problems.

topics.title: Comparing & Adding/Subtracting Mixed Fractions
topics.concept:
To compare or add unlike fractions, change them to the same denominator (the LCM) first. For mixed fractions, add or subtract the whole numbers and the fractions, regrouping when needed.

So 1½ + 2¼ = 3¾, and 3½ − 1¾ = 1¾ (after borrowing).
recap: Make denominators equal before comparing or adding unlike fractions.
Mixed fractions: work on wholes and fractions, regroup if needed.

quiz.q: Which fraction is bigger, ⅔ or ¾?

topics.title: Multiplying Fractions
topics.concept:
To multiply two fractions, multiply the numerators together and the denominators together: ½ × ⅓ = 1/6.

To multiply a fraction by a whole number, multiply the numerator by the whole number: ¾ × 8 = 24/4 = 6.
recap: Fraction × fraction: multiply tops, multiply bottoms.
Fraction × whole: multiply the numerator by the whole number.

topics.title: Dividing Fractions
topics.concept:
To divide a fraction by a whole number, multiply the denominator by that number: ½ ÷ 2 = ¼.

To divide a whole number by a unit fraction, ask how many of that fraction fit in: 3 ÷ ½ = 6, because there are 6 halves in 3.

examples.solution: There are 2 halves in each whole, so 4 ÷ ½ = 8.

recap: Fraction ÷ whole: multiply the denominator by the whole number.
Whole ÷ unit fraction: count how many fit (3 ÷ ½ = 6).

quiz.explanation: There are 2 halves in each whole, so 5 ÷ ½ = 10.

questions.q: Which is the odd one out (three are equal to ½)?
questions.explanation: 3/5 is not equal to ½; the other three are.
There are 2 halves in 1, so 1 ÷ ½ = 2.
There are 2 halves in each whole, so 4 ÷ ½ = 8.

questions.q: A 6 m ribbon is cut into ½ m pieces. How many pieces are there?
⅔ of the 30 students in a class wear glasses. How many is that?

questions.explanation: ½ × ⅔ = ⅓, and ⅓ × ¾ = 3/12 = ¼.

questions.q: A recipe needs ¾ cup of sugar. How much sugar is needed for 4 batches?
